meta.title: Dengue Tracker: Europe
meta.description: Independent, sourced tracker of locally acquired dengue in Europe in 2026: ECDC and national case counts, affected countries and clusters, the yearly trend since 2010, vaccines and a dated timeline.
meta.disclaimer: This tracker summarises ECDC, Italy's Istituto Superiore di Sanità (ISS), Santé publique France and named news reports. It is not medical or travel advice. If you develop a fever after mosquito bites or after travel, see a doctor and say where you have been.

headline: Italy has 68 locally acquired dengue cases this year and France 6, well below the 2024 record of 304.

status.label: Active · new local cases in Italy
status.summary: Italy and France are the only EU/EEA countries with locally acquired dengue this year. Italy's national health institute (ISS) counted 68 local cases in 5 outbreaks by 6 October, in places including the provinces of Livorno, Lecce and Milan and a cluster in Cartigliano (Vicenza) that had reached 8 cases by 2 October; Italy's National Blood Centre added Rome to its list of affected areas on 2 October. France counts 6 cases in 4 episodes. The total is well below the 2024 record of 304. ECDC reports weekly until November.

claims.claim: Dengue only happens in the tropics
claims.detail: Mainland Europe has had locally acquired dengue in most years since 2010, spread by tiger mosquitoes after travellers bring the virus back. The record was 304 local cases in 2024, in Italy, France and Spain.

sources.name: ECDC: local dengue in the EU/EEA, previous years

claims.claim: Dengue spreads from person to person
claims.detail: It spreads through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes, not through coughs, touch or other casual contact. Rare exceptions include mother to baby, blood transfusion or organ donation and, very rarely, sex (ECDC recorded one such case in Spain in 2019). Italy defers some blood donors from affected areas as a precaution.

claims.claim: There is no vaccine against dengue
claims.detail: Qdenga (TAK-003) has been authorised in the EU since December 2022 for people aged 4 and over. Advice on who should get it differs by country.

claims.claim: Tiger mosquitoes are now everywhere in Europe
claims.detail: ECDC's maps show the tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) established across much of southern Europe and spreading north, but not established in many northern countries. In 2026 only Italy and France have reported local dengue.

claims.claim: 2026 is Europe's worst year for local dengue
claims.detail: Not so far: 65 local cases by late September (Italy 59, France 6), against 304 in 2024 and 130 in 2023, ECDC data show.

sources.name: ECDC: local dengue in the EU/EEA, previous years

claims.claim: The risk ends when summer does
claims.detail: Cartigliano (Vicenza) has reported local cases since 25 September, and Italy's National Blood Centre added Rome to its affected areas on 2 October. In 2025 ECDC closed its season only after no new cases since late October, and it reports weekly until November this year.

timeline.title: ECDC closes the 2025 season at 35 local cases
timeline.body: France reported 29 locally acquired cases, Italy 4 and Portugal's Madeira 2. With no new cases since late October and cooler weather, ECDC ended its weekly dengue reports for the year.

timeline.title: France starts its seasonal surveillance of dengue and chikungunya
timeline.body: Santé publique France begins enhanced surveillance of dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland France for the mosquito season. Its counts of imported cases run from this date.

timeline.title: France reports its first local dengue cases of 2026
timeline.body: Two unrelated locally acquired cases are confirmed in Occitanie: one in Carmaux (Tarn) and one in Hérault.

timeline.title: France: 4 local cases, now including Dordogne
timeline.body: Santé publique France counts 3 transmission episodes with 4 cases, in Tarn, Hérault and Dordogne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine), and 308 imported dengue cases since 1 May.

timeline.title: France reaches 5 cases, now including Bouches-du-Rhône
timeline.body: Bouches-du-Rhône (Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur) is added: France has 5 locally acquired cases across Tarn, Hérault, Dordogne and Bouches-du-Rhône.

timeline.title: Italy confirms its first local outbreaks of 2026
timeline.body: The ISS counts 24 locally acquired cases by 8 September, up from 3 on 30 August, in outbreaks in Livorno province (Tuscany) and Lecce province (Puglia). The other 241 of 265 confirmed cases were linked to travel; 56% of those with a known place of infection had been in the Maldives.

timeline.title: ECDC: Italy 37 and France 5 local cases
timeline.body: As of 16 September. Italy added 13 cases in a week: 6 near Lecce, 5 near Livorno and 2 in a new cluster near Milan. France had no new cases. ECDC will report weekly until November.

timeline.title: Italy reaches 47 local cases in three outbreaks
timeline.body: The ISS links them to outbreaks in the provinces of Livorno (28 cases), Lecce (13) and Milan (2); 4 cases have no known link. 312 dengue cases have been confirmed this year, with no deaths.

timeline.title: First local case in Cartigliano, Veneto
timeline.body: A locally acquired case in Cartigliano (Vicenza) prompts mosquito control and blood-donation precautions. The local health authority reports two more cases on 29 September.

timeline.title: France: 6 local dengue cases; local chikungunya at 125
timeline.body: Santé publique France counts 4 dengue episodes with 6 cases and 424 imported dengue cases since 1 May. Separately (chikungunya, a different virus): 19 local episodes with 125 cases, including 6 in Nogent-sur-Marne (Val-de-Marne).

timeline.title: Italy: 59 local dengue cases, no deaths
timeline.body: The ISS counts 330 confirmed dengue cases from 1 January to 29 September; 59 were locally acquired and the rest linked to travel. One of 28 chikungunya cases was also locally acquired.

timeline.title: Cartigliano cluster reaches 8 cases; Rome added to affected areas
timeline.body: The local health authority reports 8 locally acquired cases in Cartigliano; one older patient is in hospital as a precaution. Italy's National Blood Centre lists Rome as an area with local dengue from 2 October.

timeline.title: Italy: 68 local dengue cases in 5 outbreaks; France unchanged at 6
timeline.body: The ISS counts 346 confirmed dengue cases from 1 January to 6 October; 68 were locally acquired, linked to 5 outbreaks plus 1 case not linked to the others, and there were no deaths. One of 29 chikungunya cases was locally acquired. Santé publique France's 7 October bulletin (data to 5 October) still counts 4 local dengue episodes with 6 cases, and 20 local chikungunya episodes with 146 cases.

facts.a: Through the bite of an infected Aedes mosquito. In Europe this is mainly the tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus), which bites during the day. A mosquito picks up the virus by biting an infected person, often a returning traveller, and can then pass it on. Dengue does not spread through casual contact.

Most infections cause mild or no symptoms. When symptoms appear, usually 4 to 10 days after the bite, they include high fever, severe headache, pain behind the eyes, muscle and joint pain, nausea and rash, and typically last 2 to 7 days.

Most people recover within one to two weeks. Some develop severe dengue, which needs hospital care; the risk is higher with a second infection by a different virus type. There is no specific treatment. Italy has reported no dengue deaths this year.
Yes. Qdenga (TAK-003) has been authorised in the EU since December 2022 for people aged 4 and over. Who is advised to get it differs by country.

facts.q: Why are there local cases in Europe?
facts.a: Travellers return with the virus from places where dengue is common, and tiger mosquitoes established in much of southern Europe can spread it locally in warm months. Local spread in Europe has been seasonal, usually ending in late autumn.
